arxiv-2201-04901.title: On inertia and ratio type bounds for the k k -independence number of a graph and their relationship
arxiv-2201-04901.creator: Aida Abiad, Cristina Dalfó, Miquel Àngel Fiol, Sjanne Zeijlemaker
arxiv-2201-04901.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Aida Abiad, Cristina Dalfó, Miquel Àngel Fiol, Sjanne Zeijlemaker. For k ≥ 1 k\geq 1 , the k k -independence number α k \alpha_{k} of a graph is the maximum number of vertices that are mutually at distance greater than k k . The well-known inertia and ratio bounds for the (1-)independence number α ( = α 1 ) \alpha(=\alpha_{1}) of a graph, due to Cvetković and Hoffman, respectively, were generalized recently for every value of k k .

arxiv-2207-00411.title: Adversarial Robustness is at Odds with Lazy Training
arxiv-2207-00411.creator: Yunjuan Wang, Enayat Ullah, Poorya Mianjy, Raman Arora
arxiv-2207-00411.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yunjuan Wang, Enayat Ullah, Poorya Mianjy, Raman Arora. Recent works show that adversarial examples exist for random neural networks ( Daniely and Shacham 2020 ) and that these examples can be found using a single step of gradient ascent ( Bubeck et al. In this work, we extend this line of work to “ lazy training ” of neural networks – a dominant model in deep learning theory in which neural networks are provably efficiently learnable.

arxiv-2306-00789.title: Improved Cross-Lingual Transfer Learning For Automatic Speech Translation
arxiv-2306-00789.creator: Sameer Khurana, Nauman Dawalatabad, Antoine Laurent, Luis Vicente, Pablo Gimeno, Victoria Mingote
arxiv-2306-00789.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sameer Khurana, Nauman Dawalatabad, Antoine Laurent, Luis Vicente, Pablo Gimeno, Victoria Mingote. Research in multilingual speech-to-text translation is topical. Having a single model that supports multiple translation tasks is desirable. The goal of this work it to improve cross-lingual transfer learning in multilingual speech-to-text translation via semantic knowledge distillation.

arxiv-2310-01691.title: Zero-Shot Continuous Prompt Transfer: Generalizing Task Semantics Across Language Models
arxiv-2310-01691.creator: Zijun Wu, Yongkang Wu, Lili Mou
arxiv-2310-01691.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zijun Wu, Yongkang Wu, Lili Mou. Prompt tuning in natural language processing (NLP) has become an increasingly popular method for adapting large language models to specific tasks. However, the transferability of these prompts, especially continuous prompts, between different models remains a challenge. In this work, we propose a zero-shot continuous prompt transfer method, where source prompts are encoded into a relative space and the corresponding target prompts are searched for transferring to target models.

arxiv-2407-07038.title: Decoding Climate Disagreement: A Graph Neural Network-Based Approach to Understanding Social Media Dynamics
arxiv-2407-07038.creator: Ruiran Su, Janet B. Pierrehumbert
arxiv-2407-07038.description: Abstract This work introduces the ClimateSent-GAT Model, an innovative method that integrates Graph Attention Networks (GATs) with techniques from natural language processing to accurately identify and predict disagreements within Reddit comment-reply pairs. Our model classifies disagreements into three categories: agree, disagree, and neutral.

arxiv-2412-01690.title: Can We Afford The Perfect Prompt? Balancing Cost and Accuracy with the Economical Prompting Index
arxiv-2412-01690.creator: Tyler McDonald, Anthony Colosimo , Yifeng Li, and Ali Emami
arxiv-2412-01690.description: Abstract As prompt engineering research rapidly evolves, evaluations beyond accuracy are crucial for developing cost-effective techniques. We present the Economical Prompting Index (EPI), a novel metric that combines accuracy scores with token consumption, adjusted by a user-specified cost concern level to reflect different resource constraints.

arxiv-2509-04115.title: A Dynamic Energy-Based Hysteresis Model for Pulsed-Operated Fast-Ramping Magnets Manuscript received July, 2025; Corresponding author: D. Moll (email: dominik.moll1@tu-darmstadt.de).
arxiv-2509-04115.creator: Dominik Moll 1 , Laura A. M. D’Angelo 1 , Herbert De Gersem 1 , Fulvio Boattini 2 , Luca Bottura 2 , Marco Gast 3
arxiv-2509-04115.description: Abstract Due to the strongly nonlinear behavior of ferromagnetic yokes, the numerical analysis of fast-ramping magnets is highly cumbersome and, therefore, in practice overly simplified by means of anhysteretic material descriptions and a posteriori loss formulae. This paper establishes the use of a dynamic ferromagnetic model combining a preconditioned energy-based hysteresis description and a thin-sheet eddy-current model in time-domain.

britannica-1911-laristan.title: Lāristān (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-laristan.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-laristan.description: Article 'Lāristān' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 16), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. It lies between 26° 30′ and 28° 25′ N. and between 52° 30′ and 55° 30′ E. and has an extreme breadth and length of 120 and 210 m. respectively, with an area of about 20,000 sq. Laristan consists mainly of mountain ranges in the north and east, and of arid plains varied with rocky hills and sandy valleys stretching thence to the coast.

pmc-10530731.creator: Junjie Liu, Shirley Wyver, Muhammad Chutiyami, Helen Little
pmc-10530731.description: The study aimed to investigate the impact of COVID-19 restrictions on children’s access to the outdoors in early childhood education and care (ECEC) settings. pmc-10547210.title: Second victim syndrome in intensive care unit healthcare workers: A systematic review and meta-analysis on types, prevalence, risk factors, and recovery time
pmc-10547210.creator: Kazuaki Naya, Gen Aikawa, Akira Ouchi, Mitsuki Ikeda, Ayako Fukushima, Shuhei Yamada, Megumi Kamogawa, Shun Yoshihara, Hideaki Sakuramoto, Amos Buh, Amos Buh, Amos Buh
pmc-10547210.description: IntroductionPatient safety incidents, including medical errors and adverse events, frequently occur in intensive care units, leading to a significant psychological burden on healthcare workers. This burden results in second victim syndrome, which impacts the psychological and psychosomatic well-being of these workers. However, a systematic review focusing specifically on this condition among intensive care unit healthcare workers is lacking.

pmc-11460880.title: Contrast-enhanced computed tomography assisted diagnosis of bleeding caused by colonic angiodysplasia: A case report
pmc-11460880.creator: Yinze Chen, Xiaomin Liu, Liang Guo, Ying Tang, Xiangwei Meng
pmc-11460880.description: Rationale:Angiodysplasia (AD) in the gastrointestinal tract is a degenerative vascular condition characterized by vascular dilation, tortuosity, and arteriovenous connections within the mucosal and submucosal layers. AD is a significant cause of lower gastrointestinal bleeding in the elderly, often presenting as chronic, intermittent hemorrhage.

pmc-12666414.title: The Predictive Value of Initial Trough Concentration of Voriconazole and Procalcitonin in Hepatotoxic Adverse Events
pmc-12666414.creator: Lijuan Chen, Xinwen Wang, Xiaoli Wu, Haiyan Qin, Hongchao Zhu
pmc-12666414.description: PurposeThis study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of initial trough concentration (Cmin) of voriconazole (VCZ) and procalcitonin (PCT) in hepatotoxic adverse events.Patients and MethodsA retrospective analysis was performed on clinical data from 170 patients administered VCZ at our institution between January 2021 and July 2025. Risk factors associated with VCZ-induced hepatotoxicity were identified through binary logistic regression analysis.

pmc-13084426.title: Implementation and effectiveness of the WHO Self-Help Plus (SH+) intervention in the Gaza Strip: a prospective hybrid type 1 non-randomised study
pmc-13084426.creator: Yasser Abujamei, Federico Tedeschi, Marianna Purgato, Giulia Turrini, Corrado Barbui
pmc-13084426.description: SummaryBackgroundSelf Help Plus (SH+) is a WHO intervention that provides strategies for managing distress arising from adversity. In the Palestinian context, SH+ holds promise in supporting psychological well-being and mitigating the impact of trauma, with the critical challenge in adapting and scaling the intervention for feasible and sustainable delivery.

pmc-13161572.title: Rational design of mechanically active RNAs: de novo engineering of functional exoribonuclease-resistant RNAs
pmc-13161572.creator: Jule Walter, Leonhard Sidl, Katrin Gutenbrunner, Denis Skibinski, Tim Kolberg, Ivo L Hofacker, Hua-Ting Yao, Mario Mörl, Michael T Wolfinger
pmc-13161572.description: Mechanically active RNAs represent an emerging class of biomolecules whose function derives from resisting molecular forces. Among them, exoribonuclease-resistant RNAs (xrRNAs) achieve this by folding into a ring-like topology that physically blocks degradation. However, despite years of structural insight, the rational design of such mechanically functional RNA devices has remained elusive.

uslaw-usc-t49-s32507.title: 49 U.S.C. § 32507 — Penalties and enforcement
uslaw-usc-t49-s32507.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t49-s32507.description: United States Code, Title 49 (Transportation); Part C (Information, Standards, And Requirements); Chapter 325 (Bumper Standards). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Civil Penalty.— (1) A person that violates section 32506(a) of this title is liable to the United States Government for a civil penalty of not more than $1,000 for each violation. A separate violation occurs for each passenger motor vehicle.
